Here's a technique I use to kill two birds with one stone: a high-intensity workout, and a meditation session. The goal of meditation is to stay in the moment to escape fear and anxiety, the goal of working out is to generate more force in less time. See the potential there?

This method works best with HIIT cardio, but it can also work well with EDT-style strength training, or really any strength training where you keep your rest periods timed, intense, and relatively short. The idea is to stay absolutely in the moment, mentally resting throughout the entire rest period, and to keep any feelings of anxiety or dread about the upcoming burst of effort from your mind. Then, at the last moment, snap yourself instantly into all-out max effort mode, and really kill it until your set or burst of effort is over. Then, go right back into a mental state of rest.

As I said before, this works best with HIIT, or with strength training where you're really pushing yourself for time. The two requirements for this are all-out full intensity exercise, and condensed/minimalized rest periods. Thus, this will not work very well with LISS cardio, or with high-rest strength and power training. I like to do it with sprints, intervals on a rower, or with a high-intensity bodyweight movement, like burpees.

It's a great way to get a little something extra out of your rest periods. This is also a great way of training yourself to control your state of mind, as you're forced to snap yourself into and out of different goals at a moment's notice. One second you're in rest, and the next second you're in attack mode. Anyone who's doing high-intensity workouts is probably doing something like this already, but it becomes all the more powerful when you really become aware of it.

So for those of you who work out but can never find the time or motivation to meditate, here's a way you can get alot of the same benefits without using any of your extra time. I hope you enjoy it.
